definitions.type: function from natural numbers to real Euclidean spaces
definitions.definition: For each natural k, Rn(k)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), the space of real k-tuples with distance (sum over j<k of |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2), with its standard Borel measurable structure. Rn(0) is the one-point space.
I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}, with the usual real metric.

definitions.type: subset of the metric product Rn(n)×ℝ
definitions.definition: Fmax=E×I. The ambient product distance between (x,t) and (y,u) is max(dist(x,y),|t-u|); use the Borel measurable structure.

definitions.type: family of coordinate maps Rn(k)×ℝ→Rn(k+1) indexed by natural k
definitions.definition: YuiJoinEquiv(k)(x,t)=(t,x_0,...,x_(k-1)) in Euclidean coordinates. This is the map defined in basis-registry.json /lean_header: identify Rn(k) with real Fin k-tuples using PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv, product with the real identity, swap factors, apply Fin.consEquivL, then the inverse PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv in dimension k+1. Its coordinate bijection is defined also at k=0; continuous linear equivalence and dimension preservation are to be justified in the metric-transfer inference, not assumed as new hypotheses.

Feuc=YuiJoinEquiv(n)''Fmax, the image of E×I in Euclidean (n+1)-space with the interval coordinate first. The interval-last realization requested by the original product notation is obtained by the coordinate permutation (t,x_0,...,x_(n-1))↦(x_0,...,x_(n-1),t).

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure H^a(A) with values in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z, subset C⊆Z and real exponent a≥0, H^a(C) is the unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure with diameter-power cost: supremum over extended scales r>0 of the infimum, over countable covers C⊆⋃_i U_i with extended diameters ediam(U_i)≤r, of Σ_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty}(ediam(U_i))^a. Here ediam is the supremum of pairwise extended distances, with ediam(∅)=0. The inner supremum is zero for an empty member. For a>0 the cost is simply Σ_i(ediam(U_i))^a. No ball-volume or exponent-dependent normalization is included. The notation H^a(C) denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a C in the frozen basis.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset C of an extended metric space Z, dimH C is its Hausdorff dimension: the infimum of positive real exponents a for which H^a(C)=0, embedded in [0,∞], with infimum of the empty set equal to ∞. In particular the empty set has dimension zero. This is the Hausdorff critical exponent convention of the frozen Mathlib dimH. A definition alone does not supply measure-dimension comparison theorems.

output.statement: For every n∈ℕ and E⊆Euclidean n-space, the Euclidean coordinate image of E×[0,1] under YuiJoinEquiv n has the same Hausdorff dimension as E×[0,1] with the max metric. The image uses interval coordinate first; moving it last is an isometric coordinate permutation. This holds at n=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary subset C of Rn(n); no nonemptiness, compactness or measurability is assumed.
Define p by moving the first coordinate to the last: p(t,x_0,...,x_(n-1))=(x_0,...,x_(n-1),t). For n=0 this is the identity on the one real coordinate.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary n and an arbitrary subset C⊆Rn(n). Define e=YuiJoinEquiv(n) by D004. It is real linear by coordinate addition and scalar multiplication, is bijective, and has inverse given by deleting the first coordinate to recover the Euclidean n-vector and taking that first coordinate as the real component. For every x∈Rn(n) and t∈ℝ, its Euclidean norm is sqrt(‖x‖²+|t|²). The nonnegative maximum of ‖x‖ and |t| is at most this norm, and the norm is at most sqrt(2) times that maximum, by comparing their squares. Thus e is bounded by sqrt(2) times the max product norm, and its inverse is bounded by the Euclidean norm. Applying these bounds to differences proves continuity of e and its inverse. Hence e is a continuous real linear equivalence between the max-norm product Rn(n)×ℝ and Rn(n+1). This also verifies directly the property of the composition specified in D004. At n=0 the empty coordinate sum is zero, and these formulas and inverse remain valid.

produces.statement: e=YuiJoinEquiv(n) is a continuous real linear equivalence from the max-norm real normed space Rn(n)×ℝ onto Rn(n+1), including n=0.

argument.text: Apply E008 with real normed spaces Rn(n)×ℝ and Rn(n+1), equivalence e from F001, and arbitrary subset C×I. It yields dimH(e''(C×I))=dimH(C×I), where the right hand product has the max metric and the left hand ambient space has its Euclidean metric. No regularity property of C is needed.

produces.statement: dimH(e''(C×I))=dimH(C×I), using Euclidean metric on the image and max metric on the product.

argument.text: Define p on Rn(n+1) by p(t,x_0,...,x_(n-1))=(x_0,...,x_(n-1),t). For any two vectors, the sum of the squares of their coordinate differences is unchanged by this finite permutation. Taking nonnegative square roots shows equality of Euclidean distances, so p is an isometry. In particular p''(e''(C×I)) is precisely the coordinate realization of C×I with the interval coordinate last. At n=0 p is the identity and this conclusion still holds.

produces.statement: p is an isometry of Rn(n+1), and p''(e''(C×I)) is the interval-last Euclidean realization of C×I; this includes n=0.

argument.text: Apply M007 to p and the Euclidean set e''(C×I), using F003. It gives dimH(p''(e''(C×I)))=dimH(e''(C×I)). Together with F002, this proves the metric-transfer equality for either coordinate order. The subset C was arbitrary, so universally closing C proves the equality for every E⊆Rn(n), without a nonempty or compact restriction. In particular H001 identifies the original current Fmax=E×I and its Euclidean image Feuc=e''Fmax, giving dimH Feuc=dimH Fmax, with the interval-last image carried by p. Universally closing n proves all clauses of the exported conclusion, including n=0. No equality of the two Hausdorff measures is asserted or used.
